annotation.method: Codex read the complete local paper, surveyed every displayed result, algorithm, error analysis, numerical experiment, conclusion, and reference, visually checked the selected source pages, searched all 24 frozen mounted object modules, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P14 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 41(4), 2021, printed pages 2311-2330

rejected_candidates.candidate: definitions (1.1)-(1.2), shifted log-sum-exp (1.3), alternative softmax (1.5), extrema notation (1.6), and floating-point model (1.7)
rejected_candidates.reason: These are definitions or setup formulas. Equation (1.4) is retained only as one anchor in the invariant package T3.
They are useful analytic results, but the selected tasks prioritize the paper's central basic-softmax computation and its exact invariants while preserving the required tier progression.
An algorithm listing is not itself a proved mathematical proposition; T1 and T2 formalize its summation stage and main softmax error result.
A faithful finite version additionally needs an elementary-function rounding model for logarithm and cancellation through log(s), which is absent from the frozen mounted objects.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3.4, alternative unshifted softmax error bound
rejected_candidates.reason: Its bound depends on the computed log-sum-exp error and exponential sensitivity; Theorem 3.3 is the cleaner central softmax result for the available frozen arithmetic surface.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithm 4.1 and Theorems 4.2-4.4 for shifted algorithms
rejected_candidates.reason: These require simultaneous models of maximum selection, subtraction, exponential, logarithm, summation, and final arithmetic. T3 captures the exact shift identity without pretending the full floating implementation is mounted.

rejected_candidates.candidate: probabilistic square-root-n improvements mentioned after Theorem 3.3
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper delegates these probabilistic results to Higham and Mary (2019, 2020) rather than proving them here.
These provide parameter data and empirical comparisons rather than universally quantified proved statements.
The recommendation summarizes the preceding analyses and experiments rather than introduce a new theorem.

T1.decision: Use the full positive exponential-evaluation and recursive-summation passage culminating in equation (3.3), retaining s, sTilde, sHat, the (n+1) coefficient, and a genuine O(u^2) remainder.

T2.decision: Use a denominator-safe exact finite componentwise certificate for the derivation and Theorem 3.3; its first-order coefficient is n+3.

T3.decision: Connect shifted formula (1.4) to the exact normalization value used in Section 5, adding the absolute-mass invariant through the frozen one-signed theorem.

selection_policy: Use results and operational invariants established or explicitly used in this paper rather than empirical plots or delegated cited results.
Preserve nonnegative exponential terms and the absence-of-overflow/underflow scope of the basic algorithm analysis.
Retain first-order O(u^2) claims as genuine asymptotic statements, with disclosed exact finite radii used only to make their remainders checkable.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
